kickCounter.title: Baby kick counter
kickCounter.subtitle: Count your baby's movements over 1 hour.
kickCounter.guidanceText: From 28 weeks, count 10 movements in under 1h, ideally after a meal. If fewer than 10 in 2h, contact your midwife or go to the maternity ward.
kickCounter.guidanceEarly: Before 28 weeks, kick counts are not yet a reliable alarm. Movements often start around 16–24 weeks. Contact your midwife if anything worries you — the 10-movements-in-2-hours rule applies from 28 weeks.
kickCounter.disclaimer: This tool is informational. It does not replace medical advice. When in doubt, contact your healthcare provider.

contractionTimer.title: Contraction timer
contractionTimer.subtitle: Measure duration and frequency of your contractions.
contractionTimer.guidanceTitle: When to go to the maternity ward?
contractionTimer.guidanceText: 5-1-1 rule: contractions every 5 min, lasting 1 min, for 1 hour. For first pregnancies. Follow your midwife's advice.
contractionTimer.disclaimer: This tool is informational. Follow your healthcare provider's advice.

hospitalBag.title: Hospital bag
hospitalBag.subtitle: Pack your bag with peace of mind.
hospitalBag.tip: 💡 Prepare your bag around 32-34 weeks. Check with your maternity ward whether they provide some items.

ramadan.title: Ramadan & Pregnancy
ramadan.subtitle: Guidance, safety, and tracking days to make up.
ramadan.draftBanner: ⚠️ Content pending clinical review. Validate with your doctor and an imam.
ramadan.consultDoctor: I consulted my doctor about fasting
ramadan.trackerSubtitle: Log non-fasted days. Islam allows you to make them up later or pay Fidya.
ramadan.disclaimer: This screen is informational. The decision to fast is yours, your doctor's, and your religious advisor's. Islam exempts pregnant women from fasting when it may harm them or their baby.

forbiddenFoodsHalal.title: Foods to avoid — halal perspective
forbiddenFoodsHalal.intro: In addition to clinical risks (listeriosis, toxoplasmosis…), here are common non-halal foods to watch during pregnancy.
forbiddenFoodsHalal.draftNote: Content pending review by an imam and a registered dietitian. Consult your doctor for dietary choices.

alcohol.label: Alcohol
alcohol.note: Forbidden in Islam and teratogenic. Includes hidden alcohol (sauces, desserts, some medications).

pork.label: Pork and derivatives
pork.note: Lard, charcuterie, pork gelatin — often hidden in candies, mass-market yoghurts, capsules.

gelatin.label: Non-halal gelatin
gelatin.note: Check origin (pork, non-zabihah beef). Found in marshmallows, gummy bears, some supplements.

nonHalalMeat.label: Non-zabihah meat
nonHalalMeat.note: Choose halal-certified meat. Salmonella risk if raw or undercooked (carpaccio, tartare).

cookingWine.label: Cooking wine/beer
cookingWine.note: Coq au vin, beer in sauces — alcohol never fully evaporates during cooking.
